text:
incident-bot: 🔔 PagerDuty: continuous-batching errors spike in us-west-2 (sev-2) — several customer sessions timing out, high 502s reported. Auto-create incident channel: #inc-2825554322

maya_oncall: I'm on it, picking up the pager. Observability shows KV cache eviction pressure and paging spikes starting ~10:45 UTC. Latency SLOs breached for some routes.

jamie_sre: linking perf dash — https://dash.internal/redwood/contbatch/us-west-2?from=10:30&to=now (watch the max_batch_tokens curve)

arjun_runtime: seeing a sudden jump in max_batch_tokens observed per-batch, lots of tiny sequences piling up, causing batching to hit memory limits and triggering aggressive KV cache eviction.

tanya_ml: any model-specific regressed? Embeddings or chat?

leo_support: early reports from two customers: chat completions stall at token 1 then error 502, some embedding jobs time out after 30s. I've opened cs tickets.

maya_oncall: quick customer-impact summary: ~12 tenants impacted intermittently, elevated error rate ~7% on chat-gen, embedding jobs latency 3-5x. No billing anomalies yet.

jamie_sre: logs show continuous-batching controller started honoring a new config rollout yesterday — suspected misconfig: max_num_seqs defaulted from 8 -> 64 in prod due to config merge.

arjun_runtime: ugh. I remember that PR, the new default was meant for GPU-dedicated hosts but landed in global config. That explains many small sequences packed into huge batches.

ines_ops: FYI I just saw paging thrash on host pool gw-9a causing disk swap churn, paging latency skyrocketed.

maya_oncall: mitigation plan — short term: revert config to previous safe values for continuous-batching, and throttle batching. Long term: fix config gating.

jamie_sre: proposed immediate hotfix: set max_num_seqs=8, max_batch_tokens=2048, request timeout bump to 2s at the batching layer for the affected pool. Canary to 3 hosts first.

arjun_runtime: agree. Also temporarily disable prefix KV-sync for the hot pool to reduce KV eviction churn.

devex_kate: can we craft a quick runnable patch and rollout playbook so SRE can apply without a full deploy?

jamie_sre: patch (will apply via runtime-config service):
```
continuous_batching {
  pools: "us-west-2:gw-*"
  max_num_seqs: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  request_timeout_ms: 2000
  prefix_kv_sync: false
}
```

maya_oncall: who can push this config now? Need fast rollback if something breaks.

arjun_runtime: I can cut the config and push to runtime-config. Will run canary on gw-9a, gw-9b, gw-9c (3 hosts).

leo_support: ETA to customers? I'll prep a customer bulletin draft to CS once we confirm reduced error rate.

arjun_runtime: pushing canary now — command: `rc push --env=prod --scope=us-west-2 --file=cb-hotfix.yaml --canary=3`

jamie_sre: monitoring: watch evictions/sec, swap usage, 5xx rate per-tenant, and per-route latency P95. Also set alert to auto-rollback if 5xx rate increases vs baseline.

incident-bot: config push started by arjun_runtime at 10:58:12 UTC — canary targets: gw-9a, gw-9b, gw-9c.

arjun_runtime: canary applied to 3 hosts. Waiting 2 minutes for stabilization.

maya_oncall: observed immediate drop in 502s on canary hosts, evictions down 70% on gw-9b. Nice.

jamie_sre: scaling metrics look much healthier. Rolling to remaining hosts in pool with a 30s interval. Proceeding.

ines_ops: rolling to rest of pool now (gw-9d..gw-9k) at low rate.

leo_support: support note: errors dropping, customers confirming better response. Sending update to affected tenants: "We're rolling a hotfix to reduce batching pressure; you may see improved response times shortly."

maya_oncall: customer impact quick note for incident report: 12 tenants affected, partial failures for ~45 minutes, error rate peaked at 7%, average extra latency 2.8x, no data loss.

jamie_sre: post-rollout check — kv cache miss rate normalized, paging latency back to baseline, no elevated swap. We'll keep the config until we ship a gated PR that prevents global default drift.

arjun_runtime: opened PR to add env-scoped defaulting and validation for continuous-batching config. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/8123

tanya_ml: we should add workload-level limits too (per-tenant max_seqs) to avoid noisy-neighbor packing. I'll coordinate with model-platform.

devex_kate: small docs note: adding a checklist for runtime-config PRs that change defaults. I'll draft and link to the incident postmortem.

maya_oncall: timeline summary for postmortem:
- 10:45 UTC — traffic spike + config drift leads to higher max_num_seqs in prod
- 10:50 UTC — KV cache eviction/paging spike observed, 502s begin
- 10:53 UTC — PD alert escalated to oncall
- 10:58 UTC — hotfix config pushed (canary 3 hosts)
- 11:02 UTC — canary stable, rolling to pool; errors decline
- 11:15 UTC — pool roll complete, metrics normalized

leo_support: any immediate customer follow-ups needed? CS asks if we can offer credits for impacted jobs.

maya_oncall: we'll include impact and mitigation in the incident report and run it by support leadership for credits. No auto-crediting yet.

jamie_sre: action items: (1) revert global default in config repo, (2) add validation to runtime-config service, (3) add per-tenant packing limits, (4) publish runbook update for continuous-batching rollbacks.

arjun_runtime: I'm owner for items 1 & 2, ETA EOD today for the config PR and guardrails.

tanya_ml: I'll own per-tenant limits design, pairing with arjun for rollout plan.

devex_kate: I'll update the ops runbook and create an internal KB: "Contbatch misconfig — hotfix & rollback steps."

maya_oncall: final status — incident resolved, SLOs restored. I'll convert to an official postmortem and assign owners. Great job triaging and fast rollback. :tada:

incident-bot: Incident closed by maya_oncall at 11:23:45 UTC — severity downgraded to sev-3 for postmortem.
